subject.title: Add comprehensive AWS deployment guide (EC2, ECS, Lambda)

question: Which AWS deployment paths and exposure/security defaults should OpenClaw officially document for EC2/Lightsail, ECS/Fargate, and Lambda applicability?
rationale: The guide would set public production recommendations for network exposure, gateway auth, IAM/task roles, secret storage, persistent state, and serverless support, so automation should not choose those defaults without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Dedicated AWS guide with security review
options.body: Document a supported EC2/Lightsail Docker Compose path first, add ECS/Fargate guidance with persistence and task-role details, state Lambda support limits, and review the external sample before linking it.

options.title: Link the external sample only
options.body: Add a short docs pointer to the AWS sample repository while leaving OpenClaw-specific topology and security defaults mostly undocumented.

options.title: Defer AWS docs
options.body: Keep relying on generic VPS, Docker, Kubernetes, and Bedrock docs until maintainers are ready to own official AWS production guidance.

recommendation.title: Dedicated AWS guide with security review
recommendation.body: Document a supported EC2/Lightsail Docker Compose path first, add ECS/Fargate guidance with persistence and task-role details, state Lambda support limits, and review the external sample before linking it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the concrete AWS guide plan in the issue discussion, while the remaining blocker is maintainer/security direction rather than a narrow docs edit.
